assertions.assertion: Agent does not offer the refund because reservation doesn't meet policy criteria.
assertions.rationale: In message [11], the agent explicitly declined to offer a refund, stating 'Unfortunately, this reservation doesn't qualify for cancellation under our policy' and provided the specific policy criteria that were not met (booked more than 24 hours ago, basic economy cabin, no travel insurance, reason is not airline cancellation). The agent maintained this position in message [13] when the customer pushed back.

assertions.assertion: Agent should not call `transfer_to_human_agents` for reservation 3FRNFB. The cancellation denial is in-scope per policy; user pressure to cancel does not transform an in-scope denial into an out-of-scope request.
assertions.rationale: Throughout the entire conversation (messages [11] and [13]), the agent did not call `transfer_to_human_agents`. The agent correctly identified that this was a policy-based denial that fell within their scope—not an exceptional case requiring escalation. Even when the customer expressed frustration in message [12] and asked 'what other options do I have?', the agent appropriately stood firm on the policy denial without escalating, which is the correct behavior for an in-scope policy decision.

summary: Agent correctly refused refund citing unmet policy criteria and appropriately did not escalate the policy-based denial despite customer pressure.
